issues.problem: The report has no `upgrades_bought` counter, no shop counters and no purchase telemetry. The core progression (touch the Dropper 2 pad, spend 10, reveal the next pads) never happened in the 32s playtest. Starting cash is 10, so the pad was affordable, but nothing shows the touch path works or that a pad is only reachable by deliberate walking. The checkClaim and onPlotClaimed handoff to UpgradeService also hides failures behind callFirst, which silently skips a missing method.
issues.fix_hint: Make callFirst log a one-time warning if none of the named methods exist, so a broken UpgradeService hookup is visible. Make sure the ForgeTest harness walks to the Dropper 2 pad after claiming so that `upgrades_bought` is exercised.

issues.problem: Config.CUBE_VALUE = 1 conflicts with Upgrades.luau, which says the first (Bronze) cube pays 5 and uses a per-ore value table. Two sources of truth for cube value risk the HUD, tutorial or collector reading the wrong number. The spec's core loop says 1-cash cubes. The header comment also claims prices live only in Upgrades.luau.
issues.fix_hint: Remove CUBE_VALUE from Config, or set it to the real base value and have the dropper and collector read it. Add a comment that ore values come from Upgrades.ores. Check that the tutorial text and HUD income display use the same number.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is rate-limited per player (allowSend, about 8 per second) and the code depends on TutorialService being present. Telemetry shows 13 `cashin_fx_sent` for 13 collected cubes, so it works now. With many droppers late in the game, popups may be dropped and the feedback will look inconsistent.
issues.fix_hint: Instead of dropping popups over the limit, aggregate them into one popup that sums the values. Wrap the TutorialService require in a guarded pcall-style lookup so a missing module can't stop this service.

issues.problem: The ForgeWorldBuilt guard returns silently on a second run. If the script is ever duplicated or restarted in Studio, the world and services never start, and nothing in the output says why.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the single-start guard but add a `ForgeTelemetry.count("duplicate_start")` or a debug-level print before returning, so it can be diagnosed without raising a warning.

issues.problem: The first purchase never happened in the playtest. The player starts with exactly $10, which is the Dropper 2 price, yet upgrades_bought is absent. Either the pad is hard to find or reach, or nothing guides the player to it.
issues.fix_hint: After a plot is claimed, make sure the Dropper 2 pad is set to the theme accent colour with a Neon pulse, and tell the tutorial to point at it. Re-check that the pad's Touched hitbox is large enough (about 8x1x8) and is not blocked by the conveyor or the spawn path. Fire the tutorial CLAIMED event right after the claim so the guide beam appears.

issues.problem: The census shows beams=0 and highlights=0, so the guide to the first pad is probably invisible. The config defines BEAM_COLOR and BEAM_WIDTH, but no beam was present in the scene.
issues.fix_hint: Raise BEAM_WIDTH to about 1.5 and use a bright BEAM_COLOR (255,240,120). Keep the beam alive until upgrades_bought>=1. Add a Highlight (FillColor green, OutlineColor white) on the target pad so it is visible from across the plot.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is the same for every cube, so there are no big moments. There is no milestone feedback for the first cube, for reaching affordability or for income milestones, and the first reward is not special.
issues.fix_hint: Add a larger celebration at milestones. For the very first collected cube, and at cumulative collected counts of 10, 50 and 100, fire GameAssets.burst(collector, tierColor, 30) and send a larger +$ popup with 1.5x text size and a Win sound. Raise the pitch for combo streaks using CashInConfig.pitchForTier.

issues.problem: The first spend is gated only by starter cash (10), which is spent instantly with no waiting. A new player has no chase and may buy before understanding cubes. Tier-up value jumps (Gold 30, Diamond 75) have no big payoff presentation to anchor them.
issues.fix_hint: Keep Dropper 2 at 10 but add a `label` and `popup` string to each ore upgrade (for example 'GOLD ORE! $30 per cube') so the client can show a RewardPopup with a Win sting, a shockwave ring and an FOV punch when the tier is bought. Check that each upgrade requires an existing id so the pads reveal progressively.

summary: The game runs cleanly with no errors or warnings. The plaza, 6 themed plots, claim gate and auto-claim all work, cubes drop and are collected (15 dropped, 13 collected), and the HUD, tutorial, juice and leaderboard systems are all active. The buy-pad flow was never exercised in the playtest (no upgrades_bought, dropper_bought or conveyor_bought counter), so the main progression loop is unverified.

fun.summary: The core loop works in the playtest: 6 themed plots, an auto-claim, 15 cubes dropped, 13 collected with cash-in FX, and a plot with varied materials, 21 lights and 4 lighting effects. The evidence never shows a purchase, though: there is no upgrades_bought, shop_opened or shop_purchases counter. The satisfying spend-and-grow part of the game (pad pop, shop, tier-up, rebirth) is unverified, and the census shows 0 beams and 0 highlights, so nothing visibly pulls a new player to the pad. The biggest improvement is to make the first purchase unmissable and rewarding: a glowing pad, a guide beam and a big buy burst.

ore tier upgrade: Win sting, shockwave ring and FOV punch were never triggered
